cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the giving is real.
cells.ask: Open the one drawer or folder you have kept as a maybe. Keep what you use. Let the rest go out this week.
cells.core:
You can hold what's heavy and hand the usable part to someone else at the same time. You know what the backup is for and how much of it to give. That share runs without any announcement, and it keeps people upright.

It also holds a season that is done. Some of what you carry, or store, or keep holding ready belongs to what has ended, and carrying it is what keeps the next thing at the door. Clearing one shelf is how this face stays strong instead of merely kind. What you give away and what you finish letting go of are the same strength spent on purpose, and that's what leaves you steady here.
cells.sheetLine: Give what is needed, and finish what has ended.
cells.verb: share the strength you have by measure
cells.place: at the completion before a new beginning

cells.tense: You are bracing against a future need that has not arrived and may not.
cells.ask: Name the ending you keep delaying. Put one hour on it today, and when the hour is done, let the rest stand until that day.
cells.core:
You're pushing support ahead of the moment that would ask for it. Extra supplies, extra availability, the whole list of what might be needed later — held ready for a day nobody named. It looks generous and feels like duty, and it drags the ending you're actually standing in behind you.

Holding without forcing is what this face looks like when it's working. The load you keep lifted ahead of time is what makes the help land wrong and turns a fair exchange into a debt you're managing. Letting the ending be an ending lets the support land where it's needed and keeps it from costing more than it gives. One hour is enough to start; the rest can wait for the day it belongs to.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you already closed.
cells.ask: Pick one object or obligation tied to what ended, finish it this week — send it back, pass it on, close the file. Then stop.
cells.core:
Something from before is still on the table. A request, a place you used to hold, an ending that never got marked — and part of your attention is still parked there. Your strength is real, and right now it stands where the old scene was.

Pushing the current scene harder doesn't reach what that unfinished thing is holding open. Finish one of those, and the help you still have to give gets its place back. The strength was not the problem; it hasn't been asked to stand anywhere current yet. When one of those endings is genuinely closed, the ground under you is this season and this season's people.
cells.sheetLine: Your strength is standing where the old room used to be.
cells.verb: share the strength you have by measure

cells.tense: You are writing without noticing you're holding the pen.
cells.ask: Say to one person what you've already given them, plainly, before you decide anything else. Then ask what they still need.
cells.core:
You have already been giving your strength outward — something moved, something got held, someone got through a stretch because you were there — and you describe it as if it just happened, or as if you were only doing your job. What goes well here is simple: help given on purpose, owned by the one who gave it, and an ending made clean when its season is over. The sharing is real. You haven't claimed it.

That claim decides where the next clearing happens and what gets kept. While it stays unspoken, the help drifts and the ending gets held longer than it needs to. One sentence to one person settles it: you did this, and here's what it was for.
cells.sheetLine: You have already been sharing it. Say so.
cells.verb: share the strength you have by measure
